note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following a dramatic PSA rise and biopsy-proven progression to ISUP Grade Group 4 prostate cancer with local extension.

This 66-year-old male is a self-employed carpenter who presents with a concerning biochemical and histological progression of his known prostate cancer. His PSA levels were previously stable, dropping to 0.7 ng/mL in March 2024, but have now surged to 8.3 ng/mL in February 2025. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms (IPSS 14/35) but denies bone pain, hematuria, or systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever. Socially, he is married but lives alone, preferring phone follow-up due to his residence being over 90 minutes from the clinic. He is a current smoker with a 30 pack-year history and consumes approximately 17 units of alcohol per week. He remains physically active, cycling five times a week for commuting. Recent audiology evaluations were conducted for hearing concerns, unrelated to his urological care. He has a history of polyneuropathy in both lower legs and is currently taking ciprofloxacin. He has no known drug allergies.

Digital rectal examination reveals a hard, irregular nodule in the right mid-base of the prostate, with loss of the median sulcus and fixation suggestive of extracapsular extension (cT3b). The abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no palpable lymphadenopathy. General examination is unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no signs of acute distress.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
